description: Installation of 1No. BT Street Hub Unit and associated advertisement panels on either side of the unit
decision_conditions: <p><span id="docs-internal-guid-73290cbf-7fff-ecaf-ecce-d95d8ce26941"><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;">The proposed advertisement would represent an incongruous visual intrusion to the street scene and contribute to an unsightly proliferation and clutter of signage and street furniture in the local area, that would detract from the visual amenity of the street scene, harm the setting of the grade ii* listed building The Hackney Empire and the character and appearance of the Town Hall Square Conservation Area. As such, the proposal would be contrary to policies D3 (Optimising Site Capacity through the Design-led Approach) and HC1 (Heritage conservation and growth) of the London Plan (2021) and policies LP1 (Design quality and local character), LP3 (Designated Heritage Assets) and LP7 (Advertisements) of Hackney's Local Development Plan (2020).</span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-b5800ca3-7fff-23ed-a4e1-1ff5630e9a79"><span style="font-size: 12pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;">The proposed advertisement, by reason of its scale, appearance, location and potential uses would result in an obstructive and intrusive form of development that would obstruct the pavement, reduce the amount of space available for use by pedestrians, block lines of sight creating blind spots and create distractions for highway users reducing the safety of the highway. As such the proposed development is contrary to policy D8 'Public Realm' and T2 'Healthy Streets' of the London Plan (2021) as well as policy PP1 'Public Realm', LP7 'Advertisements' and LP42 'Walking and Cycling' of the Hackney Local Plan.</span></span></p>
